chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

The child has a right on the father, and the father has a right on the child: The right of the father on the child is that he should obey him in every matter except in the disobedience of God, the Glorified; and the right of the child on the father is that he should give him a beautiful name, give him good training, and teach him the Qur'an.
ai.seo_question: What are the mutual rights of parents and children in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha codifies the bilateral nature of familial piety, emphasizing that a child's obedience to the father is absolute yet conditional upon not violating divine commandments. It highlights the father's educational responsibility, specifically linking moral upbringing (adab) and Quranic literacy as foundational rights of the child, reflecting the Shia emphasis on holistic spiritual and ethical development within the family unit.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 399. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

The child has a right on the father while the father too has a right on the child. The right of the father on the child is that the latter should obey the former in every matter save in committing sins of Allāh, the Glorified, while the right of the child on the father is that he should give him a beautiful name, give him good training and teach him the Qur’ān.
